title: Tenant probe & canary replay validator for usage ingest gateway
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Add a tenant-aware probing subsystem and a canary replay validator for the usage event ingestion pipeline. The goal is to proactively detect schema regressions and soft-contract changes that affect a subset of tenants before they reach production dashboards or billing. This work spans ingest-gateway v2 changes, a lightweight probe manifest format, a replay worker that runs canaries against the schema-relaxation rules engine, and Console metrics for per-tenant mismatch rates and latency breakdowns.

Background: We've seen intermittent schema drift from a small number of SDK/partner integrations; these drifts often fail silently under soft-coercion and only surface when downstream consumers rely on stricter typing. Current monitors trigger after consumer failures; this ticket moves detection earlier via proactive probes and a replay-based validator that exercises the exact codepath used by production ingestion (including prefix caching, KV policies, and routing).

Out-of-scope: global schema registry UI changes, long-term schema migration tooling, and billing pipeline changes (probing events will be explicitly excluded from billing).
acceptance_criteria: Probe manifest format documented and versioned (v1) with rule negotiation semantics
Ingest-gateway tags probe events with a provenance header (x-rw-probe:true) and excludes them from billing paths
Canary replay worker can replay last-N real events for a tenant into the validator without impacting live throughput
Console shows per-tenant mismatch rate, last-seen-schema-version, and sampled event traces for mismatches
Automated canary runs (15m cadence) trigger alerts when mismatch rate exceeds 0.5% for any tenant over 5m
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created. Added scope for tenant-aware probing and a canary replay validator to exercise schema relaxation rules.

2026-02-22 - Marco Chen: Spike complete. Prototype probe generator implemented as a thin shim in ingest-gateway; emits synthetic events derived from recent tenant schemas. Observed optional-field divergence for several embedding events; propose adding a soft-coercion policy table keyed by event-type+client-version.

2026-02-23 - Priya Nair: Reviewed prototype. Request: include deterministic provenance header and an immutable probe id for replay correlation. Also requested clearer error codes (RW_SCHEMA_MISMATCH_*) and a way to opt tenants into strict-mode canaries.

2026-02-24 - Marco Chen: Implemented provenance header x-rw-probe:true and probe_id. Added replay worker with idempotent replay (dedupe by probe_id). Pushed PR https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4891 for initial review.

2026-02-25 - SRE (J. Alvarez): Noted that adding per-tenant probe metrics increases cardinality. Suggested aggregating at tenant-namespace and sampling at 1% for low-volume tenants to control metrics cost.
2026-02-26 - Marco Chen: Addressed SRE feedback; adding sampling policy and a telemetry shard for probe metrics. Updated PR with sampling config and tracing headers for sampled events.
2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Small-scale canary scheduled (10 tenants) for 3 days. Watchlists: mismatch rate, probe-induced latency (90th), and false-positive rate vs downstream consumers.
notes:
Implementation details: probe manifests will be lightweight JSON with fields: event_type, sample_rules, optional_fields_list, canonicalized_payload_template, and expected_schema_version. The validator runs the same canonicalization and soft-coercion code as production; mismatches are logged to a separate mismatch stream for safe replay. Probe events will be routed to a quarantine topic when mismatch rate exceeds a threshold to prevent noisy cascades.

Operational plan: start with a 10-tenant internal canary, then expand to 200 tenants over 2 weeks. During canary, keep strict-mode off by default; engineering on-call will perform rapid rollbacks if false-positive mismatch spikes appear.

Rollout checklist: PR merged, small-scale canary, dashboard configured, on-call runbook updated, 2-week expansion window, GA when false-positive < 0.2% and no dashboards regression.
steps: Design probe manifest format and negotiate version semantics with schema-engineering team
Implement probe generator as a controller in ingest-gateway v2 (attach provenance headers and probe_id)
Add canary replay worker that replays tenant recent events into validator; ensure idempotence
Add per-tenant metrics and sampled traces into Console; implement sampling policy for low-volume tenants
Run 3-day small-scale canary, tune sampling and soft-coercion table, expand rollout
risks: Probe events may be routed to billing by mistake - mitigated by provenance header and explicit routing rules
High-cardinality tenant metrics could raise telemetry costs - mitigated by sampling and aggregation
Soft-coercion masking could hide breaking changes if strict-mode isn't used for major schema bumps - mitigation: strict-mode for major versions and automated regression tests
